description:
Scenario: lib.rs:291-299 implementation of get_state for unknown account returns State::from("0".to_string()). For a known account, returns the actual counter. The PLAN.md invariant (PLAN.md:139-140) says: 'State monotonicity: get_state returns a different token after every successful mutation. Token does not change on failure.'

For an unknown account, this contract says nothing. But the handler doesn't gate on account_exists before calling get_state — wait, it does (metadata.rs:305-311). So in production the unknown-account path returns accountNotFound before reaching get_state. OK, so this is internal MockBackend behavior that isn't reachable through the handler.

But the MockBackend has no test for the cross-test-account-shadowing case. Since MockBackend.create_object at lib.rs:387 calls .entry(account_id).or_default() — silently auto-registering on create — the test surface relies on this behavior. Pre-condition tests assume accounts exist when they don't. This is a divergence from MemoryBackend which is more careful (memory.rs:686-693 hard-errors on unknown account create).

Maintenance consequence: two backends with different unknown-account behavior. Tests that work against MockBackend may not work against MemoryBackend. The 'integration tests use the public MemoryBackend' policy (Cargo.toml:38-40) is correct, but the cross-shape inconsistency is a future bug magnet for contributors who try to write tests that work against both.

Fix direction: align MockBackend's unknown-account create behavior with MemoryBackend's hard-error (preferred), or document the deliberate divergence in the MockBackend rustdoc.
title: MockBackend's get_state monotonicity contract is broken: returns 0 for unknown accounts instead of the JmapBackend doc invariant
